summary: This regulation explains the rules for companies that have listed certain non-convertible securities and want to undergo a scheme of arrangement. Such companies must get a special approval letter from the stock exchange before they go to the tribunal. They must also follow specific filing steps and share documents as required.
points: Must file the draft scheme of arrangement with the stock exchange along with a fee to get a No-objection letter before filing with the tribunal.
Must not file any scheme of arrangement with the National Company Law Tribunal without first getting a No-objection letter from the stock exchange.
Must place the No-objection letter before the tribunal when asking for approval of the scheme.
Must file the draft scheme with the tribunal within six months from the date the stock exchange issues the No-objection letter.
Must submit specific documents to the stock exchange after the tribunal approves the scheme.
example: Ananta Pharma Private Limited has listed its non-convertible debt securities on the stock exchange and plans to undertake a scheme of arrangement. Before approaching the National Company Law Tribunal, Ananta Pharma files its draft scheme with the stock exchange along with the required fee to obtain a No-objection letter. Once the stock exchange issues this letter, the company makes sure to file the draft scheme with the tribunal within the six-month validity period, while also presenting the No-objection letter to the tribunal as required. After the tribunal approves the scheme, Ananta Pharma submits the necessary documents to the stock exchange.

terms.meaning: A court-approved plan between a company and its creditors or shareholders, such as a merger or restructuring.
A quasi-judicial body in India that handles corporate civil disputes and company law matters.
Debt or preference shares that cannot be converted into equity shares of the company.

watch: Remember that getting the No-objection letter from the stock exchange is a strict prerequisite before filing any scheme with the tribunal.
